newsitem.title: UK: Man Utd enjoy 7.5 mln stg European boost.
newsitem.headline: Man Utd enjoy 7.5 mln stg European boost.

text.p: English soccer club Manchester United have generated some 7.5 million stg in revenue from their success in European competition this season, chief executive Martin Edwards said on Monday.
United have reached the semifinals of the European Champions' League where they play Borussia Dortmund of Germany. The first leg is on Wednesday.

Edwards said that United's interim results included earnings of four million stg from the initial Champions' League group games. The quarter-final with Porto and semifinal meeting with Dortmund is expected to generate a further 3.5 million.
Edwards said that United would not make a lot of money should they reach the European final, a one-off match in May.

He said that ironically the club would make more money from a losing final because it would save on bonuses. However, the kudos of winning the European Cup would obviously lift merchandising income and allow United to contest the European Super Cup and World Club Championship.
Edwards does not foresee the creation of a European league in the near future.
"I personally believe that a European super league is some way off...I don't see it as an immediate thing," he said in a conference call.
Edwards said that United was talking to three companies about launching a television channel.
"We are talking to a number of companies about a Manchester United channel but we haven't decided yet whether it will be a stand-alone or part of a package with other football clubs," he said.

The Manchester United chief executive said he believe there were important questions to be resolved prior to the introduction of pay-per-view as part of the premier league's television deal with BSkyB.
Noting that the likely introduction was still two years off, Edwards said it was not clear how many matches would be screened on that basis or how the clubs would split the revenue.
United reported pre-tax profit of 19.45 million stg in the six months to end-January, the figures boosted by a 3.8 million gain on transfers.
That gain came from the sale of Lee Sharpe to Leeds United, offset by the fee paid to sign Dutchman Jordi Cruyff from Barcelona.
Edwards said that United's wage bill in the period almost doubled to more than 11.5 million stg. However, the club now employs 450 full-time staff against some 338 a year ago.

United are to spend more than 3.5 million stg on a new club museum, more than double the size of the existing venue. Edwards said the current museum had 190,000 visitors last year and could not cope with any more.
The English champions are considering opening new club stores in cities such as London, Dublin and Belfast. It is also targeting the Far East as an area where merchandising sales can be increased.
